A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Follow-Your-Shape and retain the same core method and ReShapeBench construction. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original ReShapeBench comparisons, stabilization and ControlNet ablations, qualitative editing results, and an exploratory video-editing analysis.

after.justification: V4 retains original empirical results and adds PIE-Bench comparisons, ControlNet-free results, localization diagnostics, and additional editing examples.

M1.justification: The full method retains trajectory-velocity differences, temporal aggregation, Gaussian smoothing, Otsu thresholding, three-stage KV injection, and ControlNet guidance. Evaluating a ControlNet-free ablation does not establish a revision to the proposed full method.

E1.justification: V4 adds a separate PIE-Bench evaluation of general editing, beyond the curated PIE-Bench cases already incorporated into v3's ReShapeBench mixture. Figure 17 adds examples covering material changes, color changes, and object additions. ReShapeBench construction and the exploratory video scenario remain unchanged.

E2.justification: FLUX.1 Fill is added to the qualitative comparison in Figure 6 and quantitative comparison in Table 1. The existing comparators remain: RF-Solver is relabeled RF-Edit with the same cited work and retained scores, while PnPInversion's table citation is corrected.

E3.justification: The stated ControlNet interval changes from [0.1, 0.7] to [0.1, 0.3]. Main-text denoising steps change from 28 to 14, although both appendices retain the same 15-step configuration yielding 28 function evaluations. V4 also introduces explicit full/ControlNet-free comparisons and the SAM-union and attention-map diagnostic procedures; these disclosures do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: V4 adds quantitative ControlNet-removal comparisons, a post-hoc comparison of TDM localization with SAM-derived union masks and cross-attention maps (Section 9.4), and an illustrated prompt-related failure case (Figure 11). These address additional component-attribution and localization questions. Figure 8 merely plots the retained stabilization ablation, and the video-instability analysis was already present.

E5.justification: Both versions state that random seeds are fixed and runtime is averaged across multiple trials, without specifying counts or seed values. Neither adds confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests, or other uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V4 adds PIE-Bench results for all compared methods, FLUX.1 Fill and ControlNet-free ReShapeBench results, memory measurements, and new qualitative findings. For example, the new ControlNet-free ReShapeBench PSNR is 34.85, and full-model PIE-Bench PSNR is 36.02. Existing full-model ReShapeBench scores and Table 2 values remain unchanged; the additions do not demonstrate a same-setting performance gain over v3.

T1.justification: No substantive theory, assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added. Equation 3's indexing is aligned with the already described editing window, and Algorithm 1 expands the Otsu operation using the criterion already given in Equations 5–6. These clarify existing mathematics.

C1.justification: The introduction broadens the state-of-the-art claim from ReShapeBench to both ReShapeBench and PIE-Bench, explicitly claiming effectiveness on general editing tasks. The abstract, three primary contributions, and conclusion retain the central shape-editing contribution and novelty claims.

C2.justification: V4 interprets the ControlNet-free results as showing that improvements do not depend on ControlNet and adds explanations supporting TDM's localization and interpretability. It expands prompt-failure discussion and proposes agent-based video editing, while removing v3's explicit fine-grained-editing limitation and memory-scaling warning. Memory overhead is instead characterized as manageable in the reported setting.

D1.justification: New Table 4 discloses example-specific stabilization steps and ControlNet types, intervals, and strengths. Section 9.3 adds approximately 12 GB CPU and 25 GB GPU memory usage. Global hyperparameters, hardware, the 65.3-second runtime, and the project link are retained, but v4 drops the explicit statement that ControlNet was disabled for Table 2.

R1.justification: V4 substantially expands cited literature around region editing, video generation, and agent-based editing, including ContextFlow, Follow-Your-Preference, JarvisArt, and JarvisEvo. It also removes introductory sources such as Follow-Your-Canvas, MagicStick, and COVE. The principal positioning against DiffEdit, inversion methods, and KV reuse remains; FlowEdit's publication update represents the same work.

P1.justification: ReShapeBench becomes a standalone section preceding experiments, the introduction's evaluation paragraph is rewritten, and appendix implementation and limitations sections are reorganized. Most existing methodological and benchmark prose remains. V4 also introduces duplicated 'More Editing Results' sections and makes limited affiliation, publication-note, and caption edits.

P2.justification: V4 redraws and enlarges Figure 2, revises the benchmark-construction diagram, expands Figure 6 with FLUX.1 Fill, and restructures Table 1 around two datasets and two proposed-method variants. It adds an ablation plot, localization and failure figures, an example-parameter table, and a general-editing gallery. Existing appendix galleries and video maps are retained under new numbers.

improvement.justification: The new public-benchmark and ControlNet-free comparisons strengthen empirical support, while example-specific settings and memory measurements improve reproducibility. These gains are limited by qualitative, example-based localization validation and less explicit ControlNet documentation for the unchanged stabilization table. Removing the earlier fine-grained-editing and scaling caveats also weakens the limitations discussion, but the added evidence supports a modest net improvement.
